top_story: On 30 August, the United States resumed direct strikes on Iran after weeks of pause, hitting IRGC launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz to disrupt a suspected mine-laying threat, and Tehran answered with retaliation that pushed the confrontation back into an active military cycle. Together, these tracks point to a region in which state confrontation and localized violence are reinforcing a broader climate of insecurity that civilians are increasingly forced to absorb.
